card.title: Gravity
card.text: About one-sixth of Earth's on the Moon and one-third on Mars. This matters most for mobility tests.

card.title: Air
card.text: The Moon has none and Mars has very little. This changes how hardware cools and how dust behaves.

card.title: Space radiation
card.text: Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field block it at every site.

card.title: Day length on the Moon
card.text: One lunar day lasts about 29.5 Earth days, so heating and cooling cycles are far slower.

card.title: Deep cold
card.text: Permanently shadowed lunar craters reach about -203 C ([USGS](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/astrogeology-science-center/news/artemis-iii-mission-tests-san-francisco-volcanic-field)).

card.title: Lunar dust
card.text: It is not carried by wind, so Earth dust data says little about it. The dust row applies to Mars only.

sunPanel.title: Earth's Sun
sunPanel.text: Earth's Sun crosses the sky about 30 times faster, because one lunar day lasts about 29.5 Earth days. The match is in angle, not in duration.

sunPanel.title: Earth's air
sunPanel.text: Earth's air scatters light into shadows. Lunar shadows are far darker.

sunPanel.title: lunar terrain
sunPanel.text: We do not model shadows cast by lunar terrain. That belongs to the CLPS challenge and we leave it out.
